_contract: The frozen Phase-B preregistration binds an executable-source digest. Two of its members had to change so the behavioural continuation could exist at all: the SINGLE SESSION_KIND dispatcher shared by every launchable session, and the Phase-B launcher's own preregistration gate, which now enforces the recorded-drift rule this file feeds. Recording that is the alternative to rewriting the preregistration (which would destroy the evidence of what attempt 5 executed) and to deleting the gate (which would destroy its meaning). Phase-B STAGE 1 IS COMPLETE and no further full Phase-B session is planned.
phase_b_status: STAGE 1 COMPLETE — the frozen digest is historical evidence

change.what: added a failure-path diagnostic to the CPU test gate: on a non-zero pytest result, `grep -E '^(FAILED|ERROR) ' /workspace/pytest.log` runs before the existing four-line tail
change.why: C1 attempt 3R died at this gate with `14 failed, 2650 passed` and brought home three names. The tail is four lines and /workspace/pytest.log dies with the pod, so the other eleven had to be reconstructed at $0 afterwards by guessing at the pod's environment -- and that reconstruction turned out to be partly wrong. One grep is free.
change.scope: this entry describes the CHANGE BEING DECLARED NOW. Earlier declared changes are in `history`.

why_this_is_safe_for_phase_b: A Phase-B session exports SESSION_KIND=phase_b and takes its own branch, which is byte-identical to the frozen one. The added branch is unreachable from a Phase-B session by construction.

new_runtime_module_not_in_the_frozen_set.loaded_by: autoinit_phase_b_launch.preregistration_gate, which imports it at call time
new_runtime_module_not_in_the_frozen_set.why_not_added_to_the_set: adding a member would move the digest again and is re-freezing by another name. Declared here instead, for the same reason the continuation's own source set is derived from its real import closure: a digest that omits a loaded file lets that file change without anything noticing. This module is small, has no side effects, and its own behaviour is mutation-tested.

also_affected_frozen_sets.note: the same dispatcher is a member of Phase A's harness set and the recovery continuation's. Both of those sessions are COMPLETE and their authorizations are consumed, so no live gate binds them; recorded here so the blast radius is not discovered later.

not_a_licence: This does NOT authorize further edits to the Phase-B source set. Any future change must be recorded here with the same evidence, and a change that is not additive, or that alters a pre-existing dispatch branch, must fail the gate rather than be appended to this list.

history.why: Phase C1 needs its own authorization type. Without a branch, SESSION_KIND falls through to 'spend' and loads a SpendAuthorization that refuses the C1 artifact -- the $0.2300 attempt-2 failure.
history.also_fixed: post_freeze._BRANCH matched only [a-z_]+, so a kind containing a digit was invisible: the c1 body was absorbed into the preceding branch's slice and this gate would have reported a PRE-EXISTING branch as changed, failing an additive and harmless drift. Widened to [a-z0-9_]+.

history.why: the pod CPU test gate now names every failing nodeid before it exits. No dispatch branch is touched: the change sits at the test gate, ~35 lines above the first `if [ "$SESSION_KIND" = ... ]`, and all four pre-existing branches re-hash byte-identical.
history.phase_b_impact: NONE. Phase B Stage 1 is COMPLETE, its authorization is consumed, and no further Phase-B session is planned. The changed lines execute only on a failing test gate.

measured_cumulative_numstat_vs_baseline.note: recorded because it does NOT reconcile with the first entry's `lines_added: 25, lines_removed: 0`: the 2026-08-29 change edited the Phase-B preregistration gate, which removes lines, so the cumulative drift from the baseline is not purely additive even though each declared change has been.
